LESSON: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM ZINA

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Topic 5.3: Prohibitions in Islam Zina

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Prohibitions in Islam Zina. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is Zina prohibited in Islam?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the effects of Zina on the community
2. explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society
3. appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM ZINA
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Prohibitions in Islam Zina helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM ZINA
Study Prohibitions in Islam Zina like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the effects of Zina on the community

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the effects of Zina on the community. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the effects of Zina on the community.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Prohibitions in Islam Zina” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the effects of Zina on the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Prohibitions in Islam Zina in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Prohibitions in Islam Zina is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Prohibitions in Islam Zina” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the effects of Zina on the community)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Prohibitions in Islam Zina in your own words. (skill: explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Prohibitions in Islam Zina to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the effects of Zina on the community.
3. Practise this skill: explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Prohibitions in Islam Zina from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Prohibitions in Islam Zina: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Prohibitions in Islam Zina?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is Zina prohibited in Islam?
2. How can a Muslim discourage Zina in the society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Prohibitions in Islam Zina means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the effects of Zina on the community.
5. Be able to: explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
